deduped_items.title: В Минобороны сообщили о новом боестолкновении с ВСУ в Черном море с применением авиации
deduped_items.body_text:
Российские военные уничтожили украинский безэкипажный катер. О новом боестолкновении с Вооруженными силами Украины (ВСУ) в Черном море сообщили в Министерстве обороны.
Удар по украинскому катеру в акватории Черного моря был совершен с применением морской авиации Черноморского флота.
По данным оборонного ведомства, за минувшие сутки ВСУ выпустили в сторону России 1155 беспилотников. Они также были уничтожены.
Ранее сообщалось, что в ночь с 5 на 6 августа средства противовоздушной обороны (ПВО) сбили над регионами России несколько сотен украинских беспилотных летательных аппаратов. По информации Telegram-канала «Архангел спецназа», ВСУ совершали налеты на регионы России несколькими десятками групп дронов.

deduped_items.title: ВСУ потеряли более 350 военных в зоне действий "Центра" за сутки
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Подразделения группировки "Центр" заняли более выгодные рубежи.
- Нанесено поражение живой силе и технике ВСУ в нескольких районах Донецкой Народной Республики.
- Потери украинских вооруженных формирований составили свыше 350 военнослужащих и военная техника, включая два бронетранспортера и четыре боевые бронированные машины.
МОСКВА, 6 авг - РИА Новости. Российские подразделения группировки "Центр", заняв более выгодные рубежи, уничтожили за сутки свыше 350 военнослужащих ВСУ, два бронетранспортера, четыре боевые бронированные машины, два орудия полевой артиллерии, сообщило в четверг Минобороны РФ. 
"Подразделения группировки войск "Центр" заняли более выгодные рубежи и позиции. Нанесено поражение живой силе и технике двух механизированных, егерской бригад, штурмового полка ВСУ, бригады морской пехоты и двух бригад нацгвардии в районах населенных пунктов Доброполье, Кондратовка, Новониколаевка, Анновка, Грузское, Новотроицкое и Матяшево Донецкой Народной Республики. Потери украинских вооруженных формирований составили свыше 350 военнослужащих, два бронетранспортера, четыре боевые бронированные машины, десять автомобилей и два орудия полевой артиллерии", - говорится в сообщении российского военного ведомства.
Интерактивная карта спецоперации Вооруженных сил России на Украине 
22 июня 2022, 17:18

deduped_items.title: В Москве могут ограничить работу таксистов-"зазывал"
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Заместитель руководителя департамента транспорта и развития дорожно-транспортной инфраструктуры Москвы Владимир Макаров сообщил о разработке проекта приказа, который может ограничить работу таксистов-«зазывал» в аэропорту Внуково и на железнодорожных вокзалах в Москве.
- Ограничения планируется ввести для повышения безопасности и улучшения эстетического облика вокзалов.
- Макаров подчеркнул, что запрет на работу «зазывал» поддержит легальный таксопарк и уберет нелегальные такси из указанных мест.
МОСКВА, 6 авг - РИА Новости. Работу таксистов-"зазывал" могут ограничить в аэропорту Внуково и на вокзалах в Москве, проект приказа пока обсуждается, сообщил заместитель руководителя департамента транспорта и развития дорожно-транспортной инфраструктуры Москвы Владимир Макаров. 
"В Москве на самом деле в настоящее время не такое огромное количество нарушений в этой области. Так называемые зазывалы. Когда вы выходите из аэропорта или вокзала, к вам начинают приставать люди с табличками под видом официального такси: "Я вас отвезу дешевле, чем агрегатор". Еще неизвестно, куда он этого бедного пассажира отвезет. Поэтому в настоящее время мы разработали проект приказа, в департаменте проходит стадию согласования" , - рассказал Макаров на пленарном заседании XIV Международного Евразийского форума "Такси". 
МВД предупредило о мошенничестве с заказом такси
29 июля, 08:32
Он отметил, что в отличие от других регионов, где уже действуют такие ограничения, в Москве запрет планируется ввести не только на территории крупнейшего московского аэропорта "Внуково", но и на железнодорожных вокзалах. 
Главные причины такого решения, как утверждает Макаров, заключаются в желании повысить безопасность и эстетический облик вокзалов, например Ленинградского, который недавно был отреставрирован. 
"Когда ты выходишь и видишь эти автомобили такси с заклеенными номерами и людьми, которые, соответственно, предлагают тебе условно таксомоторные перевозки, причем делают это очень навязчиво. Наверное, если это турист, то у него немножко впечатление о столице может сразу же испортиться, поэтому нельзя такого допускать", добавил он. 
Макаров также подчеркнул, что "в первую очередь, конечно же, это небезопасно". 
"Поэтому мы планируем, что введем данный запрет, и я думаю, что это будет поддержано хорошими таксопарками. Это уберет "серую" зону и нелегальные такси из этих мест", - пояснил он.
В России изменятся правила перевозки багажа в такси
2 августа, 02:39

deduped_items.title: В Дагестане пассажирка автомобиля с пьяным водителем напала на полицейского
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- В Дагестане пассажирка автомобиля с нетрезвым водителем нанесла колото-резаное ранение сотруднику Госавтоинспекции.
- Инцидент произошел утром 5 августа в Махачкале на пересечении улицы Казанбаева и проспекта Казбекова.
- Против 33-летней жительницы Махачкалы возбуждено уголовное дело по части 2 статьи 318 УК РФ.
МАХАЧКАЛА, 6 авг - РИА Новости. Пассажирка автомобиля с нетрезвым водителем в Дагестане нанесла колото-резаное ранение сотруднику Госавтоинспекции, возбуждено уголовное дело, сообщили в следственном управлении СК России по республике. 
По версии следствия, утром 5 августа на пересечении улицы Казанбаева и проспекта Казбекова в Махачкале сотрудники Госавтоинспекции остановили автомобиль для проверки документов у водителя, находившегося, по предварительным данным, в состоянии алкогольного опьянения. 
"В ходе проверки пассажир автомобиля… оказала активное сопротивление законным требованиям сотрудников полиции. В ходе противоправных действий подозреваемая применила насилие в отношении сотрудников Госавтоинспекции, причинив одному из них колото-резаное ранение левой кисти", – говорится в сообщении. 
Как уточнили РИА Новости в ведомстве, ранение женщина нанесла ключом от автомобиля 
Против 33-летней жительницы Махачкалы возбуждено уголовное дело по части 2 статьи 318 УК РФ (применение насилия, опасного для здоровья, в отношении представителя власти в связи с исполнением им своих должностных обязанностей).

deduped_items.summary: Investigators are looking for parts of a second drone believed to have hit an aircraft after an explosive-laden drone was found on a runway. Germany's interior minister has spoken of a "new level of danger." DW has more.
deduped_items.body_text:
Germany news: Search for second drone after Leipzig incident
Published August 6, 2026last updated August 6, 2026
Investigators are looking for parts of a second drone believed to have hit an aircraft after an explosive-laden drone was found on a runway. Germany's interior minister has spoken of a "new level of danger." DW has more.
What you need to know
- An investigation team is searching for a possible second drone that is believed to have hit a plane midair
- German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt described what happened as "a hybrid attack scenario"
- Western officials have repeatedly accused Russia and its proxies of staging attacks and other incidents across Europe
Here is a roundup of top stories from and about Germany on Thursday, August 6, 2026:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add DW as a Preferred Source on Google.
Industry demands action ahead of low-water talks
Ahead of Thursday's crisis talks in Bonn over exceptionally low river water levels, German industry and shipping groups are demanding concrete measures, including deepenening the river at certain points.
Holger Lösch, deputy managing director of the Federation of German Industries, told the Rheinische Post newspaper that selective deepening would allow ships to carry more cargo during periods of low water and make supply chains more resilient.
"The low-water conference in Bonn must mark the starting point for accelerating targeted deepening of the Rhine," said Lösch.
Lösch also called for more investment in waterways, arguing that Germany's transport infrastructure had been underfunded for decades.
He said planning and approval procedures also needed to be sped up significantly.
Germany's inland shipping association likewise urged the government to act.
"It is high time that the importance of rivers and canals for Germany as a business location is recognized and given greater priority."
Schwanen criticized decades of delays, noting that improving navigability of the Middle and Lower Rhine has been listed as an urgent priority in Germany's federal transport infrastructure plan since 1992.
"It is shameful that the federal government has intended for 34 years to do something for freight shipping and its customers without all that much happening," he said.
Germany calls crisis talks over extreme low river levels
German Transport Minister Steffen Bilger is holding high-level talks in Bonn today as extreme low water levels disrupt shipping on the Rhine and other rivers.
Representatives from the shipping industry, ports and businesses are due to attend the meeting around lunchtime.
"We want to assess the current situation together and take short-term action where necessary," Bilger told the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger newspaper ahead of the talks.
He said the government also wanted to draw longer-term lessons and make Germany's waterways more resilient to increasingly severe periods of low water.
Bilger is due to speak to reporters immediately after the meeting.
Low water levels are forcing inland cargo vessels to carry significantly lighter loads, pushing up transport costs and putting particular pressure on industries that rely on bulk freight.
Expert agrees Leipzig drone marks new threat level
The discovery of an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport has marked a new level of danger to critical infrastructure, agrees aviation expert Hartmut Fricke.
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt had also described the incident as a "new quality of threat" and a possible "hybrid attack scenario," an assessment with which Fricke agreed.
Unlike previous drone incidents, the danger is no longer limited to a possible collision with an aircraft or damage caused by the drone itself, the Dresden University of Technology professor told Germany's DPA news agency.
An explosive device significantly raises the potential risk, Fricke said.

Investigators are looking for parts of a second drone believed to have hit an aircraft after an explosive-laden drone was found on a runway. Germany's interior minister has spoken of a "new level of danger." DW has more.
What you need to know
- An investigation team is searching for a possible second drone that is believed to have hit a plane midair
- German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt described what happened as "a hybrid attack scenario"
- Western officials have repeatedly accused Russia and its proxies of staging attacks and other incidents across Europe
Here is a roundup of top stories from and about Germany on Thursday, August 6, 2026:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add DW as a Preferred Source on Google.
Industry demands action ahead of low-water talks
Ahead of Thursday's crisis talks in Bonn over exceptionally low river water levels, German industry and shipping groups are demanding concrete measures, including deepenening the river at certain points.
Holger Lösch, deputy managing director of the Federation of German Industries, told the Rheinische Post newspaper that selective deepening would allow ships to carry more cargo during periods of low water and make supply chains more resilient.
"The low-water conference in Bonn must mark the starting point for accelerating targeted deepening of the Rhine," said Lösch.
Lösch also called for more investment in waterways, arguing that Germany's transport infrastructure had been underfunded for decades.
He said planning and approval procedures also needed to be sped up significantly.
Germany's inland shipping association likewise urged the government to act.
"It is high time that the importance of rivers and canals for Germany as a business location is recognized and given greater priority."
Schwanen criticized decades of delays, noting that improving navigability of the Middle and Lower Rhine has been listed as an urgent priority in Germany's federal transport infrastructure plan since 1992.
"It is shameful that the federal government has intended for 34 years to do something for freight shipping and its customers without all that much happening," he said.
Germany calls crisis talks over extreme low river levels
German Transport Minister Steffen Bilger is holding high-level talks in Bonn today as extreme low water levels disrupt shipping on the Rhine and other rivers.
Representatives from the shipping industry, ports and businesses are due to attend the meeting around lunchtime.
"We want to assess the current situation together and take short-term action where necessary," Bilger told the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger newspaper ahead of the talks.
He said the government also wanted to draw longer-term lessons and make Germany's waterways more resilient to increasingly severe periods of low water.
Bilger is due to speak to reporters immediately after the meeting.
Low water levels are forcing inland cargo vessels to carry significantly lighter loads, pushing up transport costs and putting particular pressure on industries that rely on bulk freight.
Expert agrees Leipzig drone marks new threat level
The discovery of an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport has marked a new level of danger to critical infrastructure, agrees aviation expert Hartmut Fricke.
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt had also described the incident as a "new quality of threat" and a possible "hybrid attack scenario," an assessment with which Fricke agreed.
Unlike previous drone incidents, the danger is no longer limited to a possible collision with an aircraft or damage caused by the drone itself, the Dresden University of Technology professor told Germany's DPA news agency.
An explosive device significantly raises the potential risk, Fricke said.

Stattdessen will sie die Bleibeperspektiven mithilfe von Sozialpädagogen verbessern. Dieser Beitrag Westbalkanstaaten Statt abzuschieben: Köln will ausreisepflichtige Migranten unbedingt im Land behalten wurde veröffentlich auf JUNGE FREIHEIT.

deduped_items.title: Guerra ultime notizie. Raid russo nella regione di Kharkiv, tre morti a Balakliya
deduped_items.summary: Tre persone sono state uccise da un bombardamento russo su Balakliya, nella regione di Kharkiv. Lo riferice il capo dell’Amministrazione militare di Balakliya, Vitalii Karabanov, come riportato da Ukrainska Pravda....
deduped_items.body_text:
Guerra ultime notizie. Raid russo nella regione di Kharkiv, tre morti a Balakliya
Russia attacca due navi nel Mar Nero: «Trasportavano armi». Rafforzata cooperazione intelligence Kiev-Washington
3' di lettura
3' di lettura
Tre persone sono state uccise da un bombardamento russo su Balakliya, nella regione di Kharkiv. Lo riferice il capo dell’Amministrazione militare di Balakliya, Vitalii Karabanov, come riportato da Ukrainska Pravda. Secondo quanto riferito da Karabanov, il primo attacco nemico ha colpito un edificio residenziale privato, causando la morte di una donna. Sul luogo dell’incendio, i soccorritori stanno rimuovendo le macerie. Il secondo attacco nemico ha colpito nei pressi di un’altra abitazione privata. Questo attacco ha causato la morte di altre due persone: un uomo e una donna.
Chiedilo al Sole
Kiev: «Abbattuti nella notte 66 droni russi su 101, da Mosca anche quattro missili»
Durante la notte, le forze di difesa aerea ucraine hanno abbattuto 66 droni sul proprio territorio su un totale di 101 lanciati dai russi, i quali hanno anche lanciato 4 missili. In totale, 25 droni Shahed e un missile Onyx hanno colpito 18 luoghi, mentre i missili rimanenti non hanno raggiunto i loro obiettivi. L’attacco è ancora in corso. Lo scrive Ukronform, citando il bollettino mattutino dell’aeronautica militare di Kiev su Telegram. In precedenza era stato riportato che tre persone sono rimaste uccise a Balakliia, nella regione di Kharkiv, in un un attacco di droni russi.
Zelensky, colpite raffinerie russe e navi flotta fantasma
Il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky ha intanto confermato che le forze armate di Kiev hanno attaccato raffinerie russe nonché, ha detto, navi della flotta fantasma. «Oggi, le nostre sanzioni a lungo raggio hanno nuovamente contribuito a limitare i proventi petroliferi della Russia, che Mosca utilizza per finanziare la guerra e l’uccisione degli ucraini. Le Forze di Difesa ucraine hanno colpito le strutture dell’aggressore a oltre 1.300 chilometri dalla linea del fronte. La raffineria Bashneft-Novoil è stata colpita in Bashkortostan. Nella regione di Yaroslavl, a quasi 700 chilometri dal nostro confine, è stata colpita la raffineria Slavneft-Yanos. Anche le nostre risposte all’aggressione russa nel Mar Nero hanno avuto esito positivo. In particolare, sono state colpite due motovedette militari e navi della flotta fantasma», ha scritto su X il leader ucraino, ringraziando poi «tutti i combattenti che stanno ampliando sistematicamente le capacità a lungo raggio” di Kiev, “aumentando così le possibilità di una soluzione diplomatica». «La Russia deve scegliere la pace», ha concluso Zelensky.
Russia attacca due navi nel Mar Nero: «Trasportavano armi»
Mercoledì le forze armate russe hanno attaccato due navi mercantili che trasportavano rifornimenti militari a sud e a est di Odessa, nel Mar Nero. Lo ha dichiarato il Ministero della Difesa russo. «Ieri sera, droni hanno attaccato due navi mercantili che trasportavano rifornimenti militari nel Mar Nero a sud e a est di Odessa», ha affermato il ministero, così come riportato dalle agenzie di stampa russe.
Rafforzata cooperazione intelligence Kiev-Washington
Dopo la temporanea sospensione della condivisione di informazioni di intelligence nel marzo 2025, la cooperazione tra Stati Uniti e Ucraina in questo ambito non solo è stata ripristinata, ma si è anche rafforzata in modo significativo. Secondo senatori statunitensi ed esperti, ciò ha contribuito a consolidare la posizione di Kiev nel confronto con la Russia, riferisce Politico, citando alti funzionari.

La versione si concludeva con “Partigiano, portali via” e provocò la reazione dell’allora presidente di Fratelli d’Italia, che accusò Guccini di istigazione all’odio. In questo video registrato per il 25 aprile 2020, il cantautore reinterpretava “Bella ciao” citando Matteo Salvini, Silvio Berlusconi e Giorgia Meloni tra gli «invasori» contemporanei. La versione si concludeva con “Partigiano, portali via” e provocò la reazione dell’allora presidente di Fratelli d’Italia, che accusò Guccini di istigazione all’odio. deduped_items.title: Air India perde 90 metri in pochi istanti: passeggeri sbalzati contro il soffitto
deduped_items.summary: Una violenta turbolenza ha fatto perdere circa 90 metri di quota al volo Air India AI2379, partito da Phuket, in Thailandia, e diretto a Nuova Delhi. A bordo dell’Airbus A320neo viaggiavano 137 persone, tra cui tre neonati, e otto componenti dell’equipaggio. Diciassette persone sono rimaste ferite, mentre lo scossone ha danneggiato pannelli del soffitto e cappelliere. Il velivolo si è stabilizzato ed è atterrato in sicurezza a Delhi alle 11.07; la Direzione generale dell’aviazione civile indiana

deduped_items.summary: Le acque basse del Reno hanno fatto riaffiorare testimonianze di epoche in cui la siccità significava carestia. deduped_items.title: "Non rimandatemi a casa": il pianto del 12enne solo a Ceuta, simbolo del dramma dei migranti
deduped_items.summary: Un dodicenne marocchino, rimasto senza familiari durante la traversata, piange e supplica i militari spagnoli di non riportarlo oltre il confine: «Non rimandatemi a casa». La scena è avvenuta a Ceuta, città autonoma spagnola sulla costa nordafricana, travolta dal 30 luglio da un afflusso senza precedenti di circa 60 mila persone provenienti dal Marocco. Dopo l’intervento di alcune persone presenti, un ufficiale ha fermato il rimpatrio e affidato il minore alla Guardia Civil. Il suo pianto è dive

deduped_items.title: Da Hormuz a Ceuta: guerre, rotte e frontiere fragili
deduped_items.summary: In questa puntata di Breaking Point raccontiamo una settimana in cui le crisi hanno continuato ad allargarsi: dall’escalation tra Stati Uniti e Iran, con l’ingresso diretto dell’Arabia Saudita e il nuovo negoziato su Hormuz, alla visita di Netanyahu da Trump e al difficile piano per Gaza. Poi il Mediterraneo, con l’abbordaggio vicino a Pantelleria di una nave della flotta ombra russa, e infine Ceuta, dove la pressione migratoria riapre il confronto su Schengen e sugli equilibri tra Marocco, Alge

deduped_items.title: Castilla-La Mancha supera los 5.700 casos activos de violencia de género en el sistema VioGén
deduped_items.summary: Castilla-La Mancha mantiene 5.776 casos activos de violencia de género en el sistema VioGén, la herramienta del Ministerio del Interior para el seguimiento y protección de las víctimas. La cifra, actualizada a 31 de julio, sitúa a la región entre las comunidades autónomas con mayor número de mujeres incluidas en este sistema. En el conjunto del país permanecen activos 104.666 casos, de los que 1.165 presentan un nivel de riesgo alto y 14 están clasificados como de riesgo extremo , según los últi
deduped_items.body_text:
Castilla-La Mancha supera los 5.700 casos activos de violencia de género en el sistema VioGén
La comunidad registra 5.776 mujeres protegidas por el sistema de seguimiento policial del Ministerio del Interior, que contabiliza más de 104.600 casos activos en toda España
J. Guayerbas
Toledo
Castilla-La Mancha mantiene 5.776 casos activos de violencia de género en el sistema VioGén, la herramienta del Ministerio del Interior para el seguimiento y protección de las víctimas. La cifra, actualizada a 31 de julio, sitúa a la región entre las comunidades autónomas ... con mayor número de mujeres incluidas en este sistema.
En el conjunto del país permanecen activos 104.666 casos, de los que 1.165 presentan un nivel de riesgo alto y 14 están clasificados como de riesgo extremo, según los últimos datos publicados por el Ministerio del Interior.
La estadística pone de manifiesto, además, el impacto de la violencia machista sobre los menores. De los expedientes activos, 53.818 corresponden a víctimas con hijos a su cargo, mientras que en 1.664 casos los menores se encuentran también en situación de riesgo. De ellos, 149 están considerados de riesgo alto y tres de riesgo extremo.

Por comunidades autónomas, Andalucía continúa siendo la que acumula un mayor número de casos activos, con 27.885, por delante de la Comunidad Valenciana (17.111) y la Comunidad de Madrid (12.591). Investigado por el fuego de Berrocal (Salamanca) tras cortar con una radial
El fuego, originado mientras realizaba una actividad prohibida durante la época de alto riesgo de incendios, calcinó unas 214 hectáreas de pasto
H. D.
Valladolid
La Guardia Civil investiga a un varón como presunto autor de un delito de incendio forestal por imprudencia grave tras el fuego declarado el pasado 28 de julio en el término municipal de Berrocal de Huebra (Salamanca).
La investigación apunta a que el incendio se ... originó mientras el investigado realizaba trabajos de corte con una radial en una finca, una actividad expresamente prohibida en ese momento debido a la situación de alto riesgo de incendios forestales en Castilla y León.
Tras conocer los hechos, agentes del Servicio de Protección de la Naturaleza (SEPRONA) de Béjar llevaron a cabo la correspondiente inspección técnico-ocular en la zona afectada, además de identificar a las personas presentes y tomar declaración a posibles testigos.
Noticia relacionada
Como resultado de las pesquisas, determinaron que el origen del fuego se encontraba en unos trabajos realizados con una radial en la plaza de toros situada dentro de la finca. La utilización de esta maquinaria estaba prohibida al encontrarse el lugar dentro de la zona de monte y de su franja de protección de 400 metros, además de estar vigente una alerta por riesgo meteorológico de incendios forestales.
El incendio fue declarado inicialmente con un Índice de Gravedad Potencial 1 (IGR-1), al existir riesgo de afección para la población y diversas infraestructuras, aunque posteriormente fue rebajado a IGR-0 al descartarse esas circunstancias. Sin embargo, las llamas se reactivaron durante la jornada del 29 de julio y terminaron afectando a una superficie aproximada de 214 hectáreas de pasto.
Tres personas afectadas
Como consecuencia del incendio, tres personas resultaron afectadas. Dos de ellas sufrieron quemaduras leves en brazos y piernas, mientras que una tercera tuvo que ser atendida por inhalación de humo. Además, el fuego alcanzó una cabaña ganadera en la que murieron alrededor de 80 ovejas.
La Guardia Civil recuerda que entre el 12 de junio y el 12 de octubre permanece declarada la época de peligro alto de incendios forestales en Castilla y León, periodo durante el que está prohibido utilizar determinadas herramientas y maquinaria capaces de generar chispas o focos de ignición en el monte y en su zona de influencia.
En lo que va de campaña, la Comandancia de Salamanca ha investigado ya a cinco personas por delitos de incendio forestal cometidos por imprudencia grave relacionados con el uso de desbrozadoras, radiales y quemas agrícolas, además de haber detenido a otra persona como presunta autora de un incendio intencionado. Asimismo, la Guardia Civil insistió en la importancia de respetar las medidas de prevención y recordó que la colaboración ciudadana resulta fundamental para evitar este tipo de sucesos y proteger el patrimonio natural.

deduped_items.body_text:
El Gobierno transfiere casi 6,5 millones de euros a Ceuta para «reforzar» la atención a inmigrantes
Esta partida se busca «reforzar» todos los mecanismos de ayuda y acogida disponibles y «garantizar la atención sociosanitaria» de los migrantes que se encuentran tanto en el Centro de Estancia Temporal de Inmigrantes (CETI)
El Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones ha realizado una transferencia de crédito extraordinario de casi 6,5 millones de euros a Ceuta.
Según han informado fuentes del departamento que dirige Elma Saiz, con esta partida se busca «reforzar» todos los mecanismos de ... ayuda y acogida disponibles y «garantizar la atención sociosanitaria» de los inmigrantes que se encuentran tanto en el Centro de Estancia Temporal de Inmigrantes (CETI) y en sus aledaños, con «especial prioridad para quienes se encuentran en situación de mayor vulnerabilidad».
Asimismo, el Ministerio ha subrayado que las medidas que se están llevando a cabo para reforzar la red de acogida han permitido ampliar en 72 plazas el CETI de Ceuta, una ampliación que «se ha hecho efectiva gracias a la colaboración del Ministerio del Interior y Ministerio de Defensa, que ha trasladado material disponible desde el Centro de Acogida Las Raíces de Tenerife».
Noticia relacionada
El Ministerio también ha destacado que ha concertado con Cruz Roja la atención sociosanitaria de los inmigrantes que permanecen en la playa y en los alrededores del CETI, distribuyendo kits de alimentación.
La ministra Elma Saiz participa este jueves de forma telemática en un encuentro de coordinación del dispositivo de atención humanitaria en la Delegación del Gobierno de Ceuta, junto a la secretaria de Estado de Migraciones, Pilar Cancela.
Inclusión ha asegurado que sigue «muy de cerca» la situación en Ceuta y que se ha mantenido «desde el primer momento en permanente contacto y coordinación» con el Gobierno de la Ciudad Autónoma, con la Delegación del Gobierno en Ceuta, el Ministerio del Interior y con el resto de las administraciones implicadas, para «dar una respuesta humanitaria adecuada, coordinada y eficaz ante esta situación extraordinaria»

deduped_items.title: The Timeline of a Public Broadcast Appointment in the New Hungarian Dictatorship
deduped_items.summary: Péter Magyar’s Facebook governance claims another victim. As we have reported earlier this week, it took a single casual Facebook comment from Hungary’s increasingly volatile Prime Minister to remove the newly appointed Editor-in-chief of the public broadcaster’s M1 news channel. In a timeline of the events published yesterday, Gábor Hajdú gives his personal account […] The post The Timeline of a Public Broadcast Appointment in the New Hungarian Dictatorship appeared first on Hungary Today.
deduped_items.body_text:
"I do not think so", said Magyar on Facebook, triggering a panicked response from managers.Continue reading
As we have reported earlier this week, it took a single casual Facebook comment from Hungary’s increasingly volatile Prime Minister to remove the newly appointed Editor-in-chief of the public broadcaster’s M1 news channel. In a timeline of the events published yesterday, Gábor Hajdú gives his personal account of that Orwellian day early this August.
“In response to the events of the past few days, as one of the key figures in this case, I feel it is necessary to set the record straight, even though the truth only serves to confuse many people—including several opinion leaders who have reported on the matter.
First of all, I would like to state that the new leadership of public media has placed me and my family in an extremely undignified and humiliating situation, because they removed me from my position within 24 hours using the very same justification they had used to invite me to take on this honorable role.”
Namely, in both cases, they cited the need to restore the credibility of public media.”
“I left public media in 2015, after M1 became a news channel, to join Hír TV, which, starting in February of that same year ceased to be “Fidesz-aligned.” As the editor-in-chief of news programs, I strove—together with my colleagues—to achieve balance. In 2018, I did indeed move to Echo Television. After the then-management of Hír TV committed itself to Jobbik—a move I believed violated the principle of balance—I did not want to be a part of it. At Echo TV, as an editor-in-charge, I also produced news programs in accordance with the same principles, working alongside excellent colleagues who adhered to journalistic standards. Although I had not physically moved—sitting at the same desk, in the same chair—I effectively returned to Hír TV”
…Reality has slammed the door in our faces far more brutally than any prediction could have foreseen, and we are facing one of its grave consequences these days.
Instead of a sober discussion of these issues—or even the desirable role of public television—news of an appointment has devolved into a virtual lynching… Although most people are now questioning Balázs Bodacz’s (public broadcaster news director, ed. note) responsibility, it is worth noting that the entire management was fully aware of my professional background, and the CEO signed my employment contract with that knowledge. Just as space has its geometry and a place has its spirit, so too do numbers have their value and words their weight. The coordinate system for those particular 24 hours is as follows:
9:00 a.m. Signing of the employment contract at the TV headquarters on Kunigunda Way.
9:30 a.m. Meeting with the news director
10:00 a.m. Visit to the newsroom; greetings with colleagues I have not seen in a long time and new colleagues
10:30 a.m. Studio tour
11:30 a.m. Moving into the office
12:00 p.m. Branding meeting
1:30 p.m. Lunch with a former colleague
2:00 p.m. Administrative tasks, handling phone calls
5:00 p.m. Leaving the headquarters
7:42 p.m. MTI (Hungarian News Agency, ed. note) publishes the news about the appointment, which is picked up by news portals. Following this, the prime minister (Péter Magyar, ed. note) adds a comment to the news item appearing on Telex, which reads:
“I don’t think so…”
At 9:24 p.m., I receive a call informing me that I have become a burden that public media cannot bear
2:00 p.m. Signing of the termination of the employment contract
After I accepted the job offered by the management of public television—quitting my previous job to do so—they fired me without cause, taking advantage of the legal provision regarding the probationary period. I surely do not need to explain that it was not because I did something wrong on that one particular day.
If I was a propagandist because of Hír TV, then are not those who worked there at the same time as me also propagandists who no longer have a place in

deduped_items.summary: Péter Magyar’s Facebook governance claims another victim. As we have reported earlier this week, it took a single casual Facebook comment from Hungary’s increasingly volatile Prime Minister to remove the newly appointed Editor-in-chief of the public broadcaster’s M1 news channel. deduped_items.body_text:
"I do not think so", said Magyar on Facebook, triggering a panicked response from managers.Continue reading
As we have reported earlier this week, it took a single casual Facebook comment from Hungary’s increasingly volatile Prime Minister to remove the newly appointed Editor-in-chief of the public broadcaster’s M1 news channel. In a timeline of the events published yesterday, Gábor Hajdú gives his personal account of that Orwellian day early this August.
“In response to the events of the past few days, as one of the key figures in this case, I feel it is necessary to set the record straight, even though the truth only serves to confuse many people—including several opinion leaders who have reported on the matter.
First of all, I would like to state that the new leadership of public media has placed me and my family in an extremely undignified and humiliating situation, because they removed me from my position within 24 hours using the very same justification they had used to invite me to take on this honorable role.”
Namely, in both cases, they cited the need to restore the credibility of public media.”
“I left public media in 2015, after M1 became a news channel, to join Hír TV, which, starting in February of that same year ceased to be “Fidesz-aligned.” As the editor-in-chief of news programs, I strove—together with my colleagues—to achieve balance. In 2018, I did indeed move to Echo Television. After the then-management of Hír TV committed itself to Jobbik—a move I believed violated the principle of balance—I did not want to be a part of it. At Echo TV, as an editor-in-charge, I also produced news programs in accordance with the same principles, working alongside excellent colleagues who adhered to journalistic standards. Although I had not physically moved—sitting at the same desk, in the same chair—I effectively returned to Hír TV”
…Reality has slammed the door in our faces far more brutally than any prediction could have foreseen, and we are facing one of its grave consequences these days.
Instead of a sober discussion of these issues—or even the desirable role of public television—news of an appointment has devolved into a virtual lynching… Although most people are now questioning Balázs Bodacz’s (public broadcaster news director, ed. note) responsibility, it is worth noting that the entire management was fully aware of my professional background, and the CEO signed my employment contract with that knowledge. Just as space has its geometry and a place has its spirit, so too do numbers have their value and words their weight. The coordinate system for those particular 24 hours is as follows:
9:00 a.m. Signing of the employment contract at the TV headquarters on Kunigunda Way.
9:30 a.m. Meeting with the news director
10:00 a.m. Visit to the newsroom; greetings with colleagues I have not seen in a long time and new colleagues
10:30 a.m. Studio tour
11:30 a.m. Moving into the office
12:00 p.m. Branding meeting
1:30 p.m. Lunch with a former colleague
2:00 p.m. Administrative tasks, handling phone calls
5:00 p.m. Leaving the headquarters
7:42 p.m. MTI (Hungarian News Agency, ed. note) publishes the news about the appointment, which is picked up by news portals. Following this, the prime minister (Péter Magyar, ed. note) adds a comment to the news item appearing on Telex, which reads:
“I don’t think so…”

deduped_items.body_text:
"Ivan, Go Home!" Rally to Take Place Outside Russian Embassy in Prague
Prague Morning
A Czech-Ukrainian rally will take place outside the Russian Embassy in Prague on August 20 to mark the 58th anniversary of the Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia.
The event, titled “Ivan, Go Home!”, is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m. on Thursday, August 20, at Boris Němcova Square in Prague 6.
The rally comes one day before the anniversary of the night of August 20-21, 1968, when troops from five Warsaw Pact countries entered Czechoslovakia to crush the Prague Spring reform movement.
The invasion brought an end to the country’s attempt to pursue a more liberal form of socialism and was followed by two decades of political repression and Soviet military presence.
The event is being organized jointly by People in Need (Člověk v tísni), Memory of the People (Paměť národa), Million Moments for Democracy (Milion chvilek pro demokracii), and the European Congress of Ukrainians.
Organizers say the rally will connect the historical experience of the Soviet occupation with Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.
Participants will gather to remember those killed or persecuted following the 1968 invasion and the people who lived under the communist regime that followed. The organizers also plan to express support for Ukraine and draw attention to what they describe as the continuing use of imperial violence by Russia.
The choice of the rally’s name refers to one of the best-known slogans associated with the 1968 invasion. “Ivan, go home!” appeared on posters, walls, buildings and military vehicles as Czechoslovaks protested against the foreign troops occupying the country.
The invasion halted those reforms. Soviet troops remained in Czechoslovakia until the end of the communist era, while the subsequent period of “normalization” brought censorship, political purges and restrictions on civil liberties.

deduped_items.body_text:
World of Warcraft Film Ibelin to Shoot in Prague
Prague Morning
Production of Ibelin, a new film based on the life of Norwegian World of Warcraft player Mats Steen, is moving to Prague this summer.
Filming is expected to take place at Barrandov Studios from early August through early October, following the production’s spring shoot in Norway.
The film is not connected to the 2016 Hollywood movie Warcraft. Instead, it tells the real-life story of Steen, who lived with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and built friendships, relationships and a social life inside the online world of World of Warcraft.
The Prague production is reportedly seeking extras for roles including blacksmiths, guards and innkeepers. The casting suggests that parts of the film set in the game’s fictional world could be filmed in the Czech Republic. The producers have not yet officially confirmed which scenes will be shot in Prague.
Charlie Plummer leads the cast
American actor Charlie Plummer will portray Mats Steen. Toni Collette and Stephen Graham will play his parents, while the supporting cast includes Bill Nighy, Isabela Merced, Maisy Stella, John Bradley and Ivanna Sakhno.
The film will be directed by Norwegian filmmaker Morten Tyldum, whose credits include The Imitation Game and the science-fiction film Passengers.
At the center of the story is the difference between Steen’s increasingly restricted physical existence and the freedom he experienced online. His character, known in World of Warcraft as Ibelin, became an important figure to people he met through the game.
One of Norway’s largest film projects
The Prague shoot is part of an international production with a reported budget of CZK 1 billion.
According to the Norwegian Film Institute, the project received 20 million Norwegian kroner in production support.
Ibelin is being produced by Vendôme Pictures, Pathé and Neby-Tyldum as an international co-production. The Norwegian Film Institute describes it as an English-language drama with a planned running time of around two hours.
The film is being developed for theatrical release, with its premiere currently expected in the third quarter of 2027.

deduped_items.body_text:
GALLERY: Time Capsule Buried Beneath Prague's Wenceslas Square Tramline
Prague Morning
A time capsule containing different items, newspapers and messages documenting life in 2026 has been buried beneath Prague’s reconstructed Wenceslas Square.
The capsule was placed on Wednesday, August 5, near the statue of St. Wenceslas as work continues on the upper section of the square.
The Prague New Town Association, which is involved in activities around the statue and the surrounding area, organised the ceremony.
The date was not originally chosen for its historical significance. Construction work ultimately determined both the day and the location of the burial. But the association later discovered that August 5 also marks the 60th anniversary of the release of the Beatles’ Revolver album.
“We were wondering what made August 5 go down in history. Then we found out that it was 60 years ago that the Beatles released their famous album Revolver. So now we are leaving a message here for future generations,” said Monika Vlková, the association’s executive director.
The box, measuring 60 by 40 by 23.5 centimetres and weighing about eight kilograms, was then taken to a prepared pit beside the statue. Workers had excavated the hole to a depth of around 1.7 metres, where the capsule was placed before the site was covered.
The container had been wrapped in transparent protective film, as had its contents.
The collection includes coins, newspapers published during the first week of August 2026, T-shirts, badges and written messages. It also contains proposals submitted by architects during the competition for the redesign of Wenceslas Square.
The box reportedly also holds a hammer and a beer glass.
The objects are accompanied by a 20-page report describing everyday life in the Czech capital in 2026. The capsule also contains USB drives with digital material documenting the period of the Covid-19 pandemic and its effects on life in central Prague.
The capsule is intended to remain underground for decades. The association estimates that Wenceslas Square could undergo another major reconstruction in roughly 50 years, although nobody can predict when the next intervention will actually take place.

deduped_items.body_text:
"Ivan, Go Home!" Rally to Take Place Outside Russian Embassy in Prague
Prague Morning
A Czech-Ukrainian rally will take place outside the Russian Embassy in Prague on August 20 to mark the 58th anniversary of the Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia.
The event, titled “Ivan, Go Home!”, is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m. on Thursday, August 20, at Boris Němcova Square in Prague 6.
The rally comes one day before the anniversary of the night of August 20-21, 1968, when troops from five Warsaw Pact countries entered Czechoslovakia to crush the Prague Spring reform movement.
The invasion brought an end to the country’s attempt to pursue a more liberal form of socialism and was followed by two decades of political repression and Soviet military presence.
The event is being organized jointly by People in Need (Člověk v tísni), Memory of the People (Paměť národa), Million Moments for Democracy (Milion chvilek pro demokracii), and the European Congress of Ukrainians.
Organizers say the rally will connect the historical experience of the Soviet occupation with Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.
Participants will gather to remember those killed or persecuted following the 1968 invasion and the people who lived under the communist regime that followed. The organizers also plan to express support for Ukraine and draw attention to what they describe as the continuing use of imperial violence by Russia.
The choice of the rally’s name refers to one of the best-known slogans associated with the 1968 invasion. “Ivan, go home!” appeared on posters, walls, buildings and military vehicles as Czechoslovaks protested against the foreign troops occupying the country.
The invasion halted those reforms. Soviet troops remained in Czechoslovakia until the end of the communist era, while the subsequent period of “normalization” brought censorship, political purges and restrictions on civil liberties.

deduped_items.title: Hasil Babak Pertama Persija vs Arema FC: Witan Cetak Gol, VAR Gagalkan Comeback Singo Edan
deduped_items.summary: Persija dan Arema bermain imbang 1-1 pada babak pertama perebutan tempat ketiga Piala Presiden 2026. Gol Arema sempat dianulir VAR karena handsball.
deduped_items.body_text:
Piala Presiden 2026
Hasil Babak Pertama Persija vs Arema FC: Witan Cetak Gol, VAR Gagalkan Comeback Singo Edan
Persija dan Arema bermain imbang 1-1 pada babak pertama perebutan tempat ketiga Piala Presiden 2026. Gol Arema sempat dianulir VAR karena handsball.
Ringkasan Berita:
- Persija Jakarta dan Arema FC bermain imbang 1-1 pada babak pertama perebutan tempat ketiga Piala Presiden 2026. Witan Sulaeman membawa Persija unggul, sebelum Salim Tuharea menyamakan kedudukan.
- Arema FC tampil lebih dominan dengan pressing tinggi. Namun efektivitas penyelesaian akhir masih menjadi kendala bagi tim asuhan Marcos Santos.
- Arema sempat membalikkan keadaan lewat gol Marcus Vinicius pada menit ke-40. Namun, VAR menganulir gol tersebut karena lebih dulu terjadi handsball.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM - Persija Jakarta dan Arema FC bertarung sengit dalam babak pertama perebutan posisi ketiga Piala Presiden 2026, Kamis (6/8/2026) sore WIB.
Berlangsung di Stadion Kapten I Wayan Dipta, Gianyar, duel babak pertama Persija vs Arema FC sementara ini berkedudukan imbang 1-1.
Persija Jakarta berhasil unggul lebih dulu melalui aksi Witan Sulaeman pada menit ke-7.
Sementara Arema mampu menyamakan kedudukan pada menit ke-28 melalui Salim Tuharea setelah memanfaatkan kemelut di mulut gawang Persija.
Arema FC sejatinya mampu berbalik unggul pada menit ke-40 melalui sepakan Marcus Vinicius. Namun gol tersebut dianulir VAR karena terdapat pemain Arema yang handsball lebih dulu sebelum terjadi gol.
Sepanjang empat puluh lima menit babak pertama ini, Arema FC bermain lebih dominan dengan pressing tinggi dan serangan cepatnya. Namun sayangnya penyelesaian di lini depan kurang klinis.
Sementara itu, Persija di bawah asuhan Shin Tae-yong menerapkan strategi menunggu sembari melakukan counter attack saat Arema kehilangan bola.
Baca juga: Pertaruhan Harga Diri Persija vs Arema FC sebelum Cabut dari Piala Presiden 2026
Jalannya Pertama
Arema FC langsung menerapkan tempo permainan tinggi sejak peluit babak pertama dibunyikan.
Tim berjuluk Singo Edan itu langsung mengancam dari sisi kanan melalui umpan silang , namun masih mampi diantisipasi kiper muda Persija, Hafizh Rizkianur.
Sejauk lima menit jalannya awal babak pertama, Arema FC memang cukup mendominasi namun belum mampu menciptakan peluang.
Persija Jakarta justru berhasil mencetak gol lebih dulu pada menit ke-7 saat umpan trobosan Fajar Fathurrahman dari sisi kanan mampu diselesaikan Witan Sulaeman ke arah tiang dekat.
Gol, Persija unggul 1-0.
Tersengat gol cepat, Arema FC pun mencoba membangun kembali dominasi serangannya.
Gustavo Franca mencoba melepaskan tembakan spekulasi dari luar kotak penalti pada menit ke-12, namun arahnya masih melebar tipis di samping gawang Hafizh.
Hingga menit ke-25, Arema FC pun cukup mendominasi dengan pressing tinggi yang baik terbukti beberapa kali mampu mencuri bola dari pemain Persija. Namun penyelesaiannya kurang klinis.

Persija Jakarta berhasil unggul lebih dulu melalui aksi Witan Sulaeman pada menit ke-7.
Sementara Arema mampu menyamakan kedudukan pada menit ke-28 melalui Salim Tuharea setelah memanfaatkan kemelut di mulut gawang Persija.
Arema FC sejatinya mampu berbalik unggul pada menit ke-40 melalui sepakan Marcus Vinicius. Namun gol tersebut dianulir VAR karena terdapat pemain Arema yang handsball lebih dulu sebelum terjadi gol.

Arema FC langsung menerapkan tempo permainan tinggi sejak peluit babak pertama dibunyikan.
Tim berjuluk Singo Edan itu langsung mengancam dari sisi kanan melalui umpan silang , namun masih mampi diantisipasi kiper muda Persija, Hafizh Rizkianur.
Sejauk lima menit jalannya awal babak pertama, Arema FC memang cukup mendominasi namun belum mampu menciptakan peluang.
Persija Jakarta justru berhasil mencetak gol lebih dulu pada menit ke-7 saat umpan trobosan Fajar Fathurrahman dari sisi kanan mampu diselesaikan Witan Sulaeman ke arah tiang dekat.
Gol, Persija unggul 1-0.
Tersengat gol cepat, Arema FC pun mencoba membangun kembali dominasi serangannya.
Gustavo Franca mencoba melepaskan tembakan spekulasi dari luar kotak penalti pada menit ke-12, namun arahnya masih melebar tipis di samping gawang Hafizh.

deduped_items.body_text:
PSEi dips as investors await GDP data
MANILA, Philippines — Local stocks ended slightly lower on Thursday as investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of the release of the Philippines’ economic growth data, while geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continued to dampen risk appetite.
The benchmark Philippine Stock Exchange Index (PSEi) slipped 0.13 percent, or 8.36 points, to close at 6,277.95.
READ: Inflation eased further to 6.2% in July
According to Philstocks Financial Inc., investors remained cautious as they awaited the country’s gross domestic product figures, which could provide fresh clues on the strength of the local economy.
Geopolitical jitters dampen risk appetite
Uncertainty between the US and Iran also weighed on sentiment after Tehran denied reports of ongoing talks.
READ: Iran says close to Hormuz plan with Oman, but reopening depends on US
Luis Limlingan, head of sales at Regina Capital Development Corp., said a rise in unemployment in the latest labor report further dampened sentiment and raised concerns over domestic economic momentum.
“As a result, risk appetite stayed subdued, with investors opting to trim positions while awaiting clearer signals on the country’s growth outlook,” Limlingan said.
Despite the weak finish, bargain hunting in the final minutes of trading helped trim earlier losses.
Trading activity remained subdued, with net value turnover reaching P5.64 billion, reflecting the cautious mood among investors.
Foreign investors also stayed on the selling side, posting net outflows of P323.68 million.
Sectors posted mixed performance. The industrial index led the gainers after climbing 0.97 percent, while the services sector posted the steepest decline, falling 0.44 percent.
Among individual stocks, DigiPlus Interactive Corp. emerged as the session’s top performer on the benchmark index, rising 3.26 percent to P9.50.
Meanwhile, Bank of the Philippine Islands was the biggest laggard, dropping 2.32 percent to P101 per share.
Analysts said investors are likely to remain cautious in the near term as they assess incoming economic data and monitor global developments, particularly geopolitical risks that could continue to influence market sentiment. /pai

deduped_items.title: Walang Pasok: Class suspensions for August 7 due to habagat, 'Maymay'
deduped_items.summary: Several local government units have announced class suspensions for Friday, August 7, due to the continuing effects of the southwest monsoon or habagat and Tropical Depression Maymay (international name: Kujira).
deduped_items.body_text:
Walang Pasok: Class suspensions for August 7 due to habagat, 'Maymay'
MANILA, Philippines — Several local government units have announced class suspensions for Friday, August 7, due to the continuing effects of the southwest monsoon or habagat and Tropical Depression Maymay (international name: Kujira).
Maymay made landfall in Magsingal, Ilocos Sur before dawn Thursday and moved over Bangued, Abra later in the morning as it crossed Northern Luzon. By Thursday afternoon, however, PAGASA said the cyclone had weakened into a tropical depression while moving east-southeast over the Cordillera region.
Signal No. 1 remains hoisted over parts of Northern Luzon, while the weather bureau warned that the combined effects of Maymay and the southwest monsoon will continue to bring heavy rains and strong winds.
Meanwhile, PAGASA is also monitoring Typhoon Dolphin outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR).
Below is a running list of class suspensions:
Cordillera Administrative Region
- Benguet
	
  - La Trinidad – All levels, public and private
Region I (Ilocos Region)
- La Union
	
  - Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University – Classes shifted to asynchronous mode
- Pangasinan
	
  - Bugallon – All levels, public and private
  - San Carlos City – All levels, public and private
Region III (Central Luzon)
- Pampanga
	
  - San Fernando City – All levels, public and private

deduped_items.body_text:
Walang Pasok: Class suspensions for August 7 due to habagat, 'Maymay'
MANILA, Philippines — Several local government units have announced class suspensions for Friday, August 7, due to the continuing effects of the southwest monsoon or habagat and Tropical Depression Maymay (international name: Kujira).
Maymay made landfall in Magsingal, Ilocos Sur before dawn Thursday and moved over Bangued, Abra later in the morning as it crossed Northern Luzon. By Thursday afternoon, however, PAGASA said the cyclone had weakened into a tropical depression while moving east-southeast over the Cordillera region.
Signal No. 1 remains hoisted over parts of Northern Luzon, while the weather bureau warned that the combined effects of Maymay and the southwest monsoon will continue to bring heavy rains and strong winds.
Meanwhile, PAGASA is also monitoring Typhoon Dolphin outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR).

deduped_items.title: Thailand grants legal work rights to Myanmar refugees with ‘pink cards’
deduped_items.summary: NAKHON SAWAN, Aug 6 — Next to a mound of black earth, Myanmar refugees feed soil and rice seed into a clacking con...
deduped_items.body_text:
NAKHON SAWAN, Aug 6 — Next to a mound of black earth, Myanmar refugees feed soil and rice seed into a clacking conveyor machine that arranges them into ready-made planting trays for Thai farms.
The farmworkers are among their Thai boss’s newest employees, with a fresh sense of job security after Thailand began permitting Myanmar refugees living in camps to work legally and granting them non-citizen identity cards.
“I do not tire from the work. I can do it,” Ney La Jaw, 25, told AFP.
He spent much of his life confined to the Mae La refugee camp, the largest of nine temporary shelters along the border with Myanmar, according to the United Nations.
But he now lives and works more than 200 kilometres away on a farm in Thailand’s Nakhon Sawan province, earning around 3,000 baht (RM363) per week – a life-changing sum for many refugees.
“I send all of my money home to my mom” in the camp, he said.

deduped_items.title: Iran and Oman agree on new Strait of Hormuz shipping route
deduped_items.summary: TEHRAN, Aug 6 — Iran and Oman have agreed a route for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and were finalising ar...
deduped_items.body_text:
TEHRAN, Aug 6 — Iran and Oman have agreed a route for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and were finalising arrangements for jointly managing the strategic waterway, Tehran said Wednesday, even as fresh security incidents highlighted continued risks for regional shipping.
The agreement would be a step towards reopening the key energy route, but official sources briefing Iranian media stressed that any easing still hinged on Washington ending its own naval blockade of Iran’s ports.
Iran has exercised de facto control of the waterway and threatened any vessels transiting routes it deems unauthorised ever since the United States and Israel launched their war against the country on February 28.
US President Donald Trump has repeatedly insisted Tehran is keen for a deal to reopen Hormuz, but Iran has denied this and said it will instead make arrangements with its neighbour across the strait, Oman.
“The geographical coordinates of the route envisaged by the two sides have been agreed upon and, if certain third parties do not obstruct the process, the joint statement of the two countries, containing the main considerations and points of agreement, is also in the final review and drafting stage,” Iran foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said, according to state news agency IRNA.
According to the report, Baqaei told journalists that talks with Oman were moving forward, but that even if an understanding was reached, it would not mean that the strait had become safe for all passing vessels.
“The factors making the Strait of Hormuz insecure still exist on the part of the United States, particularly the naval blockade and other aggressive and threatening actions against Iran and its interests,” he said.
Highlighting the risks, the captain of an oil tanker reported hearing two explosions while transiting the strait, nine nautical miles (17 kilometres) southeast of Kumzar, Oman, Britain’s maritime security agency UKMTO said on Wednesday. The crew and vessel were safe.
Yemen’s Houthis said separately they had struck two Saudi oil tankers, the eighth and ninth hit since they launched a blockade of the kingdom last month.
Military spokesman Yahya Saree said missiles hit the tanker Wafa off Yanbu in the northern Red Sea and the tanker Daisy in the Gulf of Aden.
Saudi authorities did not immediately comment.
‘Fractured system’
Before the war, Hormuz carried around a fifth of the world’s oil and LNG exports, and prices have repeatedly surged since the dispute over the waterway erupted, piling economic and political pressure on Washington.
US Vice President JD Vance acknowledged American frustrations with the pace of diplomacy with Iran, saying negotiations would take time because of divisions within the country’s leadership.
“It’s going to be messy and it’s going to take some time to get there,” Vance told Fox News in an interview broadcast Wednesday.
“The reality... is that number one, the Iranians are extraordinarily difficult people. Number two, they have a fractured system,” he said.
After imposing an effective blockade on the strait, Iran has insisted ships take a route that hugs the Iranian coast.
Many vessels have instead chosen to take a southern route, close to Oman on the opposite side of the strait, occasionally coming under fire.
Iran wants to control the strait and charge tolls, powers it did not exercise before the war and a development that the US would fiercely oppose.
In what has become a regular pattern, Trump last week threatened to hit Iran “very hard”, potentially with attacks against civilian infrastructure, only to pull back, hinting a deal was near.
But Iran’s foreign ministry denied negotiations were taking place with Washington. — AFP

NAKHON SAWAN, Aug 6 — Next to a mound of black earth, Myanmar refugees feed soil and rice seed into a clacking conveyor machine that arranges them into ready-made planting trays for Thai farms.
The farmworkers are among their Thai boss’s newest employees, with a fresh sense of job security after Thailand began permitting Myanmar refugees living in camps to work legally and granting them non-citizen identity cards.
“I do not tire from the work. I can do it,” Ney La Jaw, 25, told AFP.
He spent much of his life confined to the Mae La refugee camp, the largest of nine temporary shelters along the border with Myanmar, according to the United Nations.
But he now lives and works more than 200 kilometres away on a farm in Thailand’s Nakhon Sawan province, earning around 3,000 baht (RM363) per week – a life-changing sum for many refugees.
“I send all of my money home to my mom” in the camp, he said.
After decades of being barred from leaving the camps and working legally, Myanmar refugees and their children began receiving non-citizen Thai ID cards in June, a step away from statelessness and towards gainful, legal employment.
About 4,600 people from Myanmar living in camps have sought permission to work legally from October 2025 to July this year, the Thai interior ministry said.
They are a fraction of the about 80,000 people who have fled conflict-torn Myanmar and live in the camps, according to UN figures.
Myanmar migrants have long toiled in neighbouring Thailand, but the country’s civil war, triggered by a 2021 military coup, has sent even more fleeing across the border.
Myanmar’s leader, ex-junta chief Min Aung Hlaing, arrived in Bangkok on Thursday, with the two nations signing an agreement on labour cooperation.
‘My own future’
In Prachinburi province, AFP journalists saw 15 displaced people collect their new ID cards at a district office in July, smiling and taking photos of the pink documents to send to their families.
“After getting the card, I don’t have to be afraid anymore when travelling around,” said Gay Lah, a Myanmar refugee who fled to a Thai camp with her family at the age of six.
She said her job as a scaffolder was tiring but going smoothly.
“I want to work hard, save money, buy a place, build a house and then bring my family out of the camp, that’s what I imagine,” she added.
Sit Nyein Aye also fled Myanmar as a child and lived most of his life “in misery” in another border camp.
Being allowed to work in construction and having an ID card gave him the chance to start fresh.
“Since I have the opportunity, I’m going out to work,” the 27-year-old said. “I have my own future.”
‘Self-reliance’
The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) welcomed Thailand’s move to issue ID cards in June, calling it a “landmark step towards inclusion, protection and self-reliance for one of the world’s most protracted refugee populations”.
Thailand’s porous borders and reputation for religious and cultural tolerance have long drawn those seeking sanctuary, but Bangkok does not legally recognise refugees or offer asylum.
However, the government began authorising legal employment for longstanding refugees last year, with more than 5,500 refugees joining the workforce since October, UNHCR said in June.
Phil Robertson, director of Bangkok-based Asia Human Rights and Labour Advocates, said the shift was a “huge step forward” and “long overdue”.
“With these so-called ‘pink cards’, the refugees can access health and other services, work to support their families, and enjoy greater freedom of movement,” he said.
Peace of mind
At the farm in Nakhon Sawan, owner Manas Lohsuwan said he had previously hired Cambodian migrants.
But since deadly border clashes between Thailand and Cambodia broke out in July last year, hundreds of thousands of Cambodian workers have returned home, leaving Manas short of labourers.
While Manas said Cambodians had more skills and experience than Myanmar refugees, the latter were cheaper to employ and required to stay with the same em

deduped_items.title: China launches probe into US cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks
deduped_items.summary: Beijing has launched a cybersecurity review into products sold in China by US technology firm Palo Alto Networks, the Cyberspace Administration of China announced on Thursday. The administration said the probe was being conducted to “ensure the secure and stable operation of critical information infrastructure, prevent cybersecurity risks and vulnerabilities, and safeguard national security”. Palo Alto Networks is a leading US cybersecurity and cloud computing provider, whose solutions are used.
deduped_items.body_text:

DevelopingChina launches probe into US cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks
The country’s cyberspace administration said the review would ‘ensure the secure and stable operation of critical information infrastructure’
1-MIN READ1-MIN
 Listen
Ji Siqiin Beijing
Beijing has launched a cybersecurity review into products sold in China by US technology firm Palo Alto Networks, the Cyberspace Administration of China announced on Thursday.
The administration said the probe was being conducted to “ensure the secure and stable operation of critical information infrastructure, prevent cybersecurity risks and vulnerabilities, and safeguard national security”.
Palo Alto Networks is a leading US cybersecurity and cloud computing provider, whose solutions are used by tens of thousands of clients in industries ranging from finance to technology and energy.
The move comes just a day after Beijing imposed sanctions on a string of US companies and tightened controls over the drone supply chain, stating the measures were a response to earlier US actions that had harmed China’s interests.
Last week, Washington effectively banned the import and sale of foreign robotic devices and power inverters – two sectors where Chinese companies are leading players – and imposed sanctions on dozens of Chinese entities.
China and the United States have been locked in an uneasy “trade truce” for months, with both sides looking to avoid a renewed tariff war while racing to “de-risk” their economies by plugging holes in their supply chains that could be weaponised by the other side.

deduped_items.title: Why was a US Yale graduate hounded out of his job promoting Chinese culture?
deduped_items.summary: In just two months, Yale graduate Edward Kuperman went from being praised by Chinese state media to being bombarded with accusations that he was a spy. It began with a June 18 article from state news agency Xinhua, in which he was described as an eager 24-year-old sinophile who made the unconventional choice of spurning China’s eastern metropolises and choosing to live in Dunhuang, in the country’s northwestern Gansu province, an oasis town on the ancient Silk Road. His interest in China started
deduped_items.body_text:
Why was a US Yale graduate hounded out of his job promoting Chinese culture?
His supposedly sky-high salary and internship at a conservative think tank sparked online fury and rumours he was a US spy
In just two months, Yale graduate Edward Kuperman went from being praised by Chinese state media to being bombarded with accusations that he was a spy.
His interest in China started with a Chinese language class in junior high, as well as books and films about China, Xinhua said. At 17, he was an exchange student in Suzhou, Jiangsu province. After returning to the US, his parents hired a Chinese tutor for him, the article said.
Kuperman, who also goes by the Chinese name Gu Aihua – “Loving China” – started his first job as an intern live-streamer at the Dunhuang Culture International Communication Centre (DCICC) in April, the article said, adding that he believed the city was a “unique entryway to observing China, understanding China and telling China’s stories.”
On his life in Dunhuang, which for centuries was a stop along the Silk Road, Xinhua’s article is typically rosy. One anecdote describes how he spent 3 hours helping a Dutch tourist find their lost backpack. “Kuperman told the relieved tourist, ‘In China, nothing gets lost.’ The tourist nodded in agreement,” the article reads.
The DCICC’s Instagram account featured Kuperman in three videos in May and June, interviewing participants at the Third World Conference of Sinologists and introducing the city’s famous Crescent Lake.

1-MIN READ1-MIN
 Listen
Ji Siqiin Beijing
Beijing has launched a cybersecurity review into products sold in China by US technology firm Palo Alto Networks, the Cyberspace Administration of China announced on Thursday.
The administration said the probe was being conducted to “ensure the secure and stable operation of critical information infrastructure, prevent cybersecurity risks and vulnerabilities, and safeguard national security”.
Palo Alto Networks is a leading US cybersecurity and cloud computing provider, whose solutions are used by tens of thousands of clients in industries ranging from finance to technology and energy.

Last week, Washington effectively banned the import and sale of foreign robotic devices and power inverters – two sectors where Chinese companies are leading players – and imposed sanctions on dozens of Chinese entities.
China and the United States have been locked in an uneasy “trade truce” for months, with both sides looking to avoid a renewed tariff war while racing to “de-risk” their economies by plugging holes in their supply chains that could be weaponised by the other side.

deduped_items.title: North Koreans turn to underground app for banned information
deduped_items.summary: North Korean authorities caught a university student in Hamhung, South Hamgyong province, this July for using illicit software that opens access to unauthorized foreign electronic materials. Demand for outside information is growing beyond simple entertainment, driven by North Koreans seeking research and technical knowledge unavailable through state channels. The software, known as the Ryongaksan Program […]
deduped_items.body_text:
North Korean authorities caught a university student in Hamhung, South Hamgyong province, this July for using illicit software that opens access to unauthorized foreign electronic materials. Demand for outside information is growing beyond simple entertainment, driven by North Koreans seeking research and technical knowledge unavailable through state channels.
The software, known as the Ryongaksan Program (named for Ryongaksan, a mountain in Pyongyang), has spread rapidly across North Korea in 2026. Authorities have launched an investigation into the program’s sellers and distribution network.
A Daily NK source in South Hamgyong province said Monday that judicial authorities caught the 21-year-old student in mid-July. He had installed the Ryongaksan Program on his mobile phone in Hamhung. The investigation found he bought the program in Pyongyang for $30. Authorities are now tracking down the seller and the distribution route, the source said.
Judicial authorities confiscated the student’s phone. They also plan to seize funds held in the phone’s e-wallet app, on the grounds that the money was used to distribute unauthorized materials, according to the source.
How the Ryongaksan Program works
The Ryongaksan Program lets users search and view external electronic materials stored within it, even while offline, the source said. North Korean IT technicians are believed to have modified similar overseas programs to fit conditions inside the country. The exact developers and the makeup of the installation files remain unconfirmed.
The program reportedly contains entertainment content alongside a large volume of foreign academic papers and technical materials. It is spreading quickly among university students, graduate students and technicians.
“It’s difficult to write academic papers or learn new technology using only materials provided by the state,” the source said. “So this program has drawn particular attention from university students, graduate students and technicians. It’s popular because it includes materials that are hard to obtain inside North Korea, such as advanced foreign construction technology and specialized agricultural data on fertilizer management for different crops.”
North Korean people generally cannot freely access the internet. Access to domestic intranets such as Gwangmyong and Mirae (North Korea’s tightly restricted, closed-loop domestic computer networks) is also strictly limited in scope and eligibility. Against this backdrop, the spread of the Ryongaksan Program reflects strong internal demand to access quality electronic materials freely, without needing a network connection.
City party threatens legal punishment
The Hamhung city party committee issued a directive on July 18 to institutions, enterprises, working organizations and neighborhood watch units. It warned that individuals who reproduce, sell or distribute state-unapproved books and electronic materials will face strong legal punishment, according to the source.
The city party defined mass reproduction or distribution of unauthorized materials as an anti-state act. It said it would hold the heads of relevant units jointly responsible if such incidents occur, the source said.

The Ryongaksan Program lets users search and view external electronic materials stored within it, even while offline, the source said. deduped_items.title: Texts suggest Angus Taylor ‘paid money to the Reformers … or was refusing to’, Icac inquiry hears
deduped_items.summary: Jean-Claude Perrottet, brother of former NSW premier, asked about messages referencing federal opposition leader and factional group ReformersIcac’s spotlight has shone on Dominic Perrottet’s brother – and it won’t be the last we hear from his familyNew South Wales’ anti-corruption watchdog has been shown text messages which suggest Angus Taylor “had paid some money to the Reformers … or was refusing to”, according to the lawyer assisting the inquiry.Taylor, the federal opposition leader, is not
deduped_items.body_text:
New South Wales’ anti-corruption watchdog has been shown text messages which suggest Angus Taylor “had paid some money to the Reformers … or was refusing to”, according to the lawyer assisting the inquiry.
Taylor, the federal opposition leader, is not named in Icac’s allegations and has previously denied making payments to the hard-right factional group the Reformers.
Jean-Claude Perrottet, a member, was on Thursday read text messages sent by Reformer cofounder Christian Ellis in September 2021. Ellis says the group has “zero dollars at the moment” in one message.
Jean-Claude asks why and Ellis replies: “Because Michael O’Hara hates the vax campaign, and Angus Taylor hates Rob.”
The counsel assisting Icac, Juliet Curtin, asked: “That seems to be suggesting that Mr Taylor had paid some money to the Reformers too, doesn’t it, or was refusing to?”
Jean-Claude replied: “It sounds like that’s the suggestion.” Curtin then said: “Do you know anything about that?”
“Look, I’ve heard it come up [at the inquiry], but until that came up, I hadn’t recalled that at all,” the younger brother of the former NSW premier Dominic Perrottet said.
Dominic Perrottet is not named in Icac’s allegations and is not accused of wrongdoing.
The inquiry has previously heard evidence, including from Reformers cofounder Robert Assaf, that hotelier Michael O’Hara threatened to end an arrangement in which he paid lobbying company Beckington for Reformers factional work after the group adopted an anti-vaccination stance.
Inquiry hears intercepted calls
Late on Thursday, the inquiry heard intercepted phone calls from fugitive property developer Jean Nassif for the first time since the opening day of the inquiry.
The corruption watchdog is examining an allegation that between 2020 and 2023, Nassif and his company Toplace made prohibited donations solicited or accepted by Ellis, Jeremy Greenwood and Charles Perrottet in exchange for the pursuit of outcomes sought by Nassif.
They including the damage to the career of former Liberal minister and Baulkham Hills MP David Elliott and the removal of the then building commissioner David Chandler, but the inquiry has yet to focus extensively on the allegation.
On Thursday afternoon, Jean-Claude Perrottet was played three phone calls between him and Nassif in 2021, when he was managing shares for Nassif while working at Medallion Financial.
In one call, Nassif can be heard asking Jean-Claude Perrottet to withdraw “100” from his portfolio to give to “to your brother, to Jeremy or Chris” for “preselection”.
Asked about which brother Nassif was proposing to give $100,000, Jean-Claude Perrottet said he didn’t know.
“I don’t know what he’s talking about, to be honest with you,” he said, rejecting the suggestion the money was to support the Reformers recruitment work, describing the call as “nonsense”.
He was played another call, previously heard on the first day of the inquiry, in which Nassif can be heard to claim that he “fucked him [David Elliott] sideways”, forcing “the boys” to get rid of the former Liberal MP’s seat of Baulkham Hills, and had sent “Castle Hill fucking hundreds of new members”.
Jean-Claude Perrottet described the call, in which he also thanked Nassif for “all the support for the family”, as “nonsensical”.
“That’s a throwaway comment that gets used all the time,” he said of his remark to Nassif about his family, saying he was not aware of Nassif providing financial support to bring new Liberal members to the Castle Hill branch.
He described a third phone call, in which Nassif complained about Chandler, who had been scrutinising his developments for defects, as “crazy talk”.
In the call, Nassif allegedly said he “had been promised that the commissioner will be fucking stopped or chased or fucking done something to him”, asking if Jean-Claude Perrottet “can take a message to Charlie or to Dom, the building commissioner, we need to stop him”, and making a subsequent request to “get Charlie to do something pleas

deduped_items.body_text:
Advertisement
DevelopingChina launches probe into US cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks
The country’s cyberspace administration said the review would ‘ensure the secure and stable operation of critical information infrastructure’
1-MIN READ1-MIN
 Listen
Ji Siqiin Beijing
Beijing has launched a cybersecurity review into products sold in China by US technology firm Palo Alto Networks, the Cyberspace Administration of China announced on Thursday.
The administration said the probe was being conducted to “ensure the secure and stable operation of critical information infrastructure, prevent cybersecurity risks and vulnerabilities, and safeguard national security”.
Palo Alto Networks is a leading US cybersecurity and cloud computing provider, whose solutions are used by tens of thousands of clients in industries ranging from finance to technology and energy.
The move comes just a day after Beijing imposed sanctions on a string of US companies and tightened controls over the drone supply chain, stating the measures were a response to earlier US actions that had harmed China’s interests.
Last week, Washington effectively banned the import and sale of foreign robotic devices and power inverters – two sectors where Chinese companies are leading players – and imposed sanctions on dozens of Chinese entities.
China and the United States have been locked in an uneasy “trade truce” for months, with both sides looking to avoid a renewed tariff war while racing to “de-risk” their economies by plugging holes in their supply chains that could be weaponised by the other side.
